This is goal g-33a7a4ae, round 2 (fix round; round 1 was audit-only and already merged as docs/state/silent-failures.md; several fix batches already merged for other files). Read that doc's methodology section first (top of file) and the per-file section for tools/server-discovery.mjs (search for '### tools/server-discovery.mjs' - it lists exact line numbers, all try-catch-no-binding).

This file discovers running swarm board/remote-serve processes by reading OS process/network info (e.g. /proc entries, command lines) - a best-effort discovery scan, not a gate or control path. For EACH flagged line in tools/server-discovery.mjs only (do not touch any other file, do not fix findings in other files even if you notice them while reading):

1. Read the surrounding function to understand what the catch is actually guarding against and what happens today when it swallows silently (what does the function return/do next - likely 'skip this candidate and keep scanning the rest').
2. Decide, from the real code, whether this catch is:
   (a) An EXPECTED/benign condition - e.g. a /proc entry or file that may not exist (ENOENT) because the process already exited mid-scan, a permission-denied (EACCES/EPERM) read of another user's process info, a malformed/unreadable entry that should just be skipped. For these, keep the swallow (do not change control flow or add noisy logging for the expected path), but narrow to the specific expected error code(s) and add minimal visibility (see point 3) for anything else unexpected - same return value, same behavior, just visible.
   (b) A genuinely UNEXPECTED-error catch with no narrower expected case. Add minimal visibility only: a one-line log. This file has no existing logger/journal convention of its own - use `console.error('[tools/server-discovery.mjs] <short context naming the function/operation>:', error?.message ?? error)`. Do NOT add a throw, do NOT change the function's return value or control flow, do NOT change what happens next.
3. If a catch binds no error variable, add a REAL binding and actually reference it in a console.error call - do not just rename-and-ignore a binding.

Do not refactor anything beyond the flagged catch blocks. Do not reformat unrelated code. Do not rename functions or change exports. Preserve every existing behavior path exactly except for the narrowing/visibility described above - a process that exited mid-scan or a permission-denied read must still be silently skipped, never thrown, since scanning many processes and some disappearing or being unreadable is entirely normal.

Your workspace does not include the test suite, so you cannot run it yourself - the orchestrator runs the real full suite against your output after integration and will send back any regression as a follow-up. List, in your final summary, which of the 7 flagged lines you narrowed (case a) vs. just added logging to (case b), with one line each.
